title: Production and Concentration of Recombinant Lentiviral Particles
protocol: Prepare a 0.0004% solution of poly-L-lysine in water and filter sterilize using a 0.22 μm filter.
Apply poly-L-lysine solution to each plate and incubate at room temperature for at least 2 hours, agitate occasionally.
Warm appropriate cell culture medium, PBS, and Opti-MEM in a 37 °C water bath.
Aspirate the poly-L-lysine solution from each plate.
Rinse the plates three times with ddH₂O immediately before adding cells and transfection mix.
Do not allow the plates to dry during rinsing.
Prepare appropriate volume of transfection mixes in separate 50 mL tubes as indicated in the attached table.
Incubate Mix 1 separately for 5 minutes.
Incubate Mix 2 separately for 5 minutes.
Combine Mix 1 and Mix 2 and incubate for an additional 20 minutes.
During the 20-minute incubation, follow steps 2-13 of the section “Sub-culturing cells” of the SOP for 293T splitting.
Resuspend cells to a concentration of approximately 2.0 x 10^6 cells/mL in growth medium.
In a 15cm plate, add fresh growth medium (add 6.75mL for 15cm plate or 2.75mL for 10cm plate).
Add DNA-Lipofectamine 2000 complexes in Opti-MEM to the plates.
Incubate cells in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO₂ for 24 hours.
Aspirate the transfection medium into a flask containing bleach.
Gently add fresh growth medium to each plate of transfected cells.
Incubate cells in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO₂ for 48 hours.
Begin collection of viral particles at approximately 10:00 AM.
Centrifuge the conditioned medium at 1000 x g in a tabletop centrifuge for four minutes to pellet cellular debris.
Filter the supernatants through a filter.
Use a 0.45 µM pore syringe filter to remove small particulate debris.
Add 11 mL of each viral supernatant to ultracentrifuge tubes.
Weigh the viral supernatant in the ultracentrifuge tube using a balance.
Fill remaining ultracentrifuge tubes with ddH2O for balancing purposes.
Spin at 50,000 x g (20,000 RPM in a Sorvall TH-641 rotor) for 2 hours and 20 minutes at 20 °C.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Treat the discarded supernatant with bleach before disposal.
Resuspend the pellet in the medium of the target cells by vigorous trituration.
Resuspend concentrated viral particles from a single plate with 1 mL of target cell growth medium.
Pellet insoluble material at top speed in a microcentrifuge for two minutes.
Transfer the supernatant(s) to new tube(s).
Aliquot viral supernatant into cryotubes as 50 μL aliquots.
Store the aliquoted viral supernatants at -80 °C.
